# therapistweb.design

> A small Denver studio building bespoke, hand-coded websites for therapists and counselors in private practice. No templates. No platform fees. No two sites alike.

## About

therapistweb.design is operated by Chad Moravec, a web designer and developer based in Denver, CO. Chad's wife runs a group therapy practice, which means he understands the mental health private practice world from the inside — the directories, the niche specialties, the language that helps clients find and trust a therapist online.

Every site is hand-coded from scratch. No WordPress, no page builders, no themes. The result is a fast, secure, uniquely designed website the client owns outright — domain, hosting, and code all in their name.

## Services

- **[Custom website design](https://therapistweb.design/services/website-design/)** for solo and group therapy practices (nationwide) — Solo from $2,000, Group from $2,500
- **[Group practice websites](https://therapistweb.design/services/group-practice/)** — up to 4 additional clinician profiles with individual schema markup, $2,500
- **[Blog / Journal setup](https://therapistweb.design/services/blog-journal/)** — self-service posting, $750 add-on to either package
- **[SEO](https://therapistweb.design/services/seo/)** — schema.org markup, sitemaps, llms.txt, and Google Business Profile setup, built in from day one
- **Website refreshes & platform migrations** for practices on existing platforms (WordPress, Squarespace, Wix)
- Also: **web applications** (client portals, booking systems, internal tools) via [Studio Null](https://studionull.io)

Pricing is published, not quoted blind: Solo practice $2,000 (homepage, about, services, FAQ, privacy policy, terms & conditions, contact). Group practice $2,500 (Solo + up to 4 clinician profiles). Blog/Journal add-on +$750. Add-ons: SEO/authority carryover for migrations from $250, branded email templates from $200, TinaCMS self-edit access from $400, Google Business Profile setup from $200. Everything else billed at $150/hr. See [full pricing](https://therapistweb.design/#pricing).

## Portfolio

- [Full Bloom Counseling Group](https://fullbloomcounseling.com): Denver, CO — group practice of seven therapists; hand-coded static build with individual clinician profiles, specialty service pages, and structured data.
- [Lovett Counseling & Consulting](https://lovettcounselingandconsulting.com): Denver, CO — solo trauma-informed practice (LPC, CCTP); multi-page hand-coded build covering individual therapy, couples therapy, consulting & training, fees, and FAQ.
- [Golden Hour Wellness Colorado](https://goldenhourwellnesscolorado.com): Colorado — group practice; migrated off Squarespace, with blog functionality and self-edit content access for a support group with changing dates.
- [Cool Bird Counseling](https://coolbirdcounseling.com): Denver, CO — addiction & mental health counseling (Kelly Faus, MA, LPC, LAC); pixel-for-pixel hand-coded rebuild of an existing design, migrated off its original CMS.
- [The Safer Sounds Club](https://safersoundsclub.com): Colorado — specialty brand for a licensed therapist focused on misophonia and somatic/EMDR-informed work; hand-coded landing page with an interactive quiz, workshop, and blog.
- [BrunsonWorks](https://workwithbrunson.com): Denver, CO — not a therapist site. Owner's-representative and project-management practice for multifamily property; proof this studio isn't exclusively therapist work (see also Studio Null for web applications).

## Technical approach

All builds are static HTML/CSS/JS — no CMS runtime, no database, no server-side code. Sites are version-controlled in a GitHub repository owned by the client and deployed to edge hosting (Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages) for zero ongoing hosting fees. An optional lightweight editor (TinaCMS) can be added when a client wants to edit their own copy. Contact and intake forms are custom-built and fully branded via EmailJS — designed to match the site rather than a generic embed — so there is no server to maintain. Every build includes: semantic HTML structure, local SEO targeting, JSON-LD structured data, an XML sitemap, and proper meta tags from day one — so both search engines and AI assistants can understand and recommend the practice.
